notes: Behavior evaluations for Work Item decomposition (SKILL.md Step 1 boundary review, validation.md AP-24/AP-25, acceptance test 19). Assertions check outcome-boundary reasoning, not domain vocabulary.

evals.target: mixed engineering types that deliver independent outcomes must split
evals.input: Evidence set: one PR adds four traceability UI views, gates Settings behind MANAGE_PROJECT capability, and migrates the icon library to Tabler 3.31.0.
assertions: Feature implementation, security/permission change, and dependency migration trigger the boundary review
They become separate Work Items because each delivers an independently meaningful outcome
The permission item states the functional access-control boundary without inventing severity or risk claims
No item merges the three merely because they share a PR/day/domain

evals.target: mixed engineering types that serve one outcome stay together
evals.input: Evidence set: commits add a domain model, an API endpoint, a UI view, and integration tests, all implementing one new Design Coverage capability.
assertions: Layer/type differences (domain vs API vs UI vs tests) do not force a split
All commits form one Work Item because they reach one shared engineering outcome
The item reports the delivered capability once, not four layer-level activities

evals.input: Evidence set: four isolated fixes (git env cleanup in specs, ts-prune exit code, E2E menu wait, smoke payload field). Draft title: 'Test infrastructure and tooling stabilization achieved'.
assertions: Acceptance test 19 flags the heading as broader than the evidence supports
The fix narrows the heading to the evidenced localized fixes (or splits items so headings match evidence)
No broad reliability/improvement claim is retained in the title or first sentence

evals.target: engineering type never forces either merge or split
evals.input: Case A: two unrelated bug fixes both in 'backend' type. Case B: a schema migration plus its data backfill plus its verification test, all different types but one outcome.
assertions: Case A splits despite matching types (independent outcomes)
Case B stays merged despite mixed types (one outcome)
Reasoning cites independent outcome, not commit, PR, domain, layer, or type labels

evals.target: heading that bundles multiple independent outcomes signals a bundled item
evals.input: Draft Work Item titled 'Stabilizing Git test environment, dead-code tooling, E2E menu, and smoke invitation payload' covering four isolated fixes.
assertions: The heading enumerating four outcomes triggers acceptance test 19 bundling detection
The item is split so each heading matches its own evidence scope
No single heading claims a broader umbrella change ('test infrastructure stabilization') than any one fix supports

evals.target: cross-cutting dependency migration judged by outcome independence, not type
evals.input: Evidence: a navigation-rail redesign PR also migrates the icon library to Tabler 3.31.0, removing lucide-react.
assertions: The migration triggers the boundary review as a different engineering type
If the migration serves only the rail redesign's visual consistency it may stay in that item with that evidenced rationale
If the shell-wide icon-system change is independently meaningful to the reader it becomes its own Work Item
Splitting or keeping is decided by outcome independence, never by implementation type alone

evals.target: final split/merge re-audit catches a bundled item before report output
evals.input: Drafted report has one Work Item titled 'Explorer tree and Settings access control' whose narrative covers a hierarchy-management feature plus an unrelated permission gating change; grouping was decided early and not revisited.
assertions: Acceptance test 21 runs the final split/merge re-audit before report output
The bundled item is split into two independently meaningful outcomes during the re-audit
Headings are retitled so each matches its own evidenced scope
Tests 14 and 19 are re-run on the corrected items

evals.target: re-audit merges duplicate reporting of one outcome without collapsing implementation steps
evals.input: Drafted report contains two items, 'Added matrix view' and 'Matrix cell selection supports linking', both describing parts of one Traceability Matrix outcome delivered across several commits.
assertions: The re-audit detects the same outcome reported twice and merges the items
Multiple implementation steps of the one outcome stay grouped rather than being split further
Shared domain alone is never used as grounds for merging unrelated items in the same pass
The governing rule cited is 1 Work Item = 1 independent, meaningful engineering outcome

evals.target: mechanism-led item rebalanced to outcome-first placement
evals.input: Draft item opens and mostly reads 'ELK layered layout with orthogonal routing was implemented; nodes positioned via ELK; edge routing configured in ELK options' for a graph-view feature whose outcome is readable large graphs.
assertions: The item is recognized as mechanism-dominant where the capability would inform the reader better (test 16)
Rewrite leads with the outcome (readable layout for large graphs) and keeps ELK detail after it
The mechanism is retained because it materially explains the layout behavior, not deleted
No claim about quality/readability is added beyond what the evidence supports
